problem_text:
A logistics company needs to coordinate 5 delivery trucks across 5 distribution centers.

Each truck follows a predetermined route represented as (Distribution Center, Unloading time) pairs,
where each pair specifies the distribution center where unloading must occur and the time required for unloading.
The sequence of pairs indicates the mandatory order in which the distribution centers must be visited.

Truck routes:
* Truck 1 follows: (DC1, 1) → (DC2, 3) → (DC4, 2) → (DC5, 7) → (DC3, 4)
* Truck 2 follows: (DC5, 4) → (DC4, 6) → (DC3, 10) → (DC1, 2) → (DC2, 10)
* Truck 3 follows: (DC1, 5) → (DC3, 1) → (DC2, 9) → (DC4, 1) → (DC5, 4)
* Truck 4 follows: (DC3, 4) → (DC1, 5) → (DC4, 5) → (DC2, 5) → (DC5, 9)
* Truck 5 follows: (DC4, 1) → (DC3, 5) → (DC2, 9) → (DC5, 2) → (DC1, 1)

Each unloading operation must proceed without interruption once initiated,
and each distribution center can only accommodate one truck at a time for unloading.
The objective is to schedule all unloading operations at the distribution centers
so that the total completion time for all delivery routes is minimized.
